class.name: NetwPersistenceBook
class.brief_description: Which entities the session persists, and the engine that persists each one.
class.description: The registry half of persistence, kept apart from the snapshot machinery the way [NetwSnapshotBook] is kept apart from the columns it accumulates. An entity is addressed by its RID rather than by its wrapper, so a row cannot be reached through an object that was freed and cannot be lost when the wrapper is re-minted. A row that named a dead wrapper would keep flushing a body nobody owns. [method entities] answers in ENROLMENT order and that order is the contract, not an accident: a flush is a write per entity and a stable order is what makes two runs of the same session produce the same transaction sequence. [codeblock] book.enroll(entity.rid, engine) false when the entity already had one book.engine_of(entity.rid) null where nothing is enrolled for rid in book.entities(): enrolment order, stable across runs book.engine_of(rid).flush() [/codeblock]

method.name: clear
method.description: Forgets every enrolment, which is what a session end owes: an engine that outlived its session would flush into a database the next session never opened.

method.name: drop
method.description: Removes [param entity]'s enrolment and answers whether there was one. The caller flushes BEFORE dropping where a last snapshot window is owed; this book takes no position on that, because whether a departure deserves a final write is the departure's question rather than the registry's.

method.name: engine_of
method.description: The engine enrolled for [param entity], or [code]null[/code] where nothing is. Answering null rather than minting one is deliberate: minting is a decision about whether the entity is persisted at all, and it belongs to the caller that knows the entity's configuration.

method.name: enroll
method.description: Enrolls [param engine] for [param entity] and answers [code]true[/code] only for a FRESH enrolment. A second enrolment replaces the engine and answers [code]false[/code], so a caller can tell "I registered this" from "this was already registered" without a separate query. An invalid [param entity] or a null [param engine] enrolls nothing and answers [code]false[/code].

method.name: entities
method.description: Every enrolled entity, in enrolment order. Safe to iterate while dropping rows, because it is a copy.

method.name: group_by_database
method.description: Batches the tick's due writes so each database is committed ONCE. [param due_rows] is one dictionary per due entity, each naming its database under [code]db[/code], and each answered batch is the INDICES into [param due_rows] that share one database. Indices rather than the rows themselves, so the caller keeps whatever it paired them with (the engine that has to be told the write committed) without that pairing crossing here. Both orders are the contract. Databases come back in first-appearance order and rows within a database in arrival order, which is what makes two runs of one session produce the same transaction sequence. A row naming no database joins no batch, because a write with nowhere to go is not a write, and no due rows answer no batches rather than one empty one. This is the batching that makes the gather cost worth paying: two hundred entities sharing one database cost one commit per tick instead of two hundred.
